title: Built an MMORPG in 30 days using AI
author: ElioSprung_7
selftext:
I have always like MMORPGs like Ragnarok Online for their simple visuals, social gameplay and the feeling of a living world

About a month ago I started a personal experiment using AI as the main production tool instead of building everything manually. I have over 20 years of experience in software and game systems so I focused on architecture and design while AI handled most of the implementation

AI was used to generate code, art, animations, audio and content. I iterated on gameplay systems and overall structure

After 30 days I had a playable multiplayer prototype. It included a persistent world with character classes and progression, real time combat against monsters, quests and exploration zones, plus trading, chat and basic economy systems including crafting

The main takeaway is that AI did not replace design work. It mainly sped up execution. Most of the effort still went into refining systems and deciding what to build next. Curious how other developers see this approach and whether it changes how they evaluate AI-assisted games

comments.author: juniperbush12
comments.body: I like that your takeaway wasn't "AI replaced developers" but "AI sped up execution" That feels much closer to how most experienced developers are actually using these tools

replies.author: ElioSprung_7
replies.body: Yeah that distinction matters. AI as a force multiplier for people who know what they're building versus magic wand that does design for you. Experience is what lets you actually use it well

comments.author: TaroBlends
comments.body: What I'd be curious about is how maintainable the project feels after a month. Getting a prototype working is one thing but keeping an AI-generated codebase organized as it grows seems like the real long term challenge

replies.author: BenMakesGames
replies.body:
it's true of human-made code, too; I feel the solution is the same: listen to your devs and let them do refactoring tickets!

I have Claude write & implement tickets, documenting pain points while it implements + a skill that looks over recently-completed tickets to find recurring pain points, which I create tickets from. I've also started using Cursor's "thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review" skill after most tickets. a few months in, and I'm still cruisin' with my game (though my few months could be the same as someone else's one month - depends on how much free time you've got :P)

replies.author: ElioSprung_7
replies.body: That's the real test. Fast iteration for a month is easy. Maintaining coherent architecture once things actually scale is where most projects fall apart, AI or not. Difference is with AI code you need even stricter upfront planning since you can't rely on consistency as features compound

replies.author: Specialist_Set1921
replies.body:
The real question if the network code is even usable for an actual player mass. 

He didn't tell us how he handles the serverload, realm managment and so on. 

Network code is really hard even for experienced devs. Remember new world which was a flop because their experienced devs fucked up the network code.

GenAi has a reputation to be especially bad in security issues. So I wouldn't be suprissed if this mmo is riddled with it.

comments.author: the_mosthated
comments.body: A multiplayer prototype in 30 days is impressive. I'm curious how the networking help up once you had multiple players interacting because that seems to be where AI-generated projects usually run into the hardest problems

comments.author: Zamaxan1
comments.body:
That’s essentially how I’ve use it for my project.  I’ve handled design/“big picture” mechanics and guiding gameplay/system design.

It’s allowed me to very quickly troubleshoot and see how different features affect gameplay in essentially realtime as opposed to spending hours potentially formatting coding for something I already know what to do for.

comments.author: FarBarnacle2468
comments.body: Inspired alot! I always want to build my own game but many things blocked that path...

replies.author: ElioSprung_7
replies.body: Wha kind of things were blocking you? The execution part is what shifts with AI, so if it was time or technical depth that was the wall, that's what changes

comments.author: DocHolidayPhD
comments.body: Sure... But is it of any such quality that anyone would play it. For an MMORPG, to truly fit that genre, it must be truly "massive" and in that case you need player volume. Otherwise you've created a sandbox which is far easier and may even be kinda meaningless.

comments.author: Orehruoy99
comments.body:
Yeah lots of YouTube videos of one prompt having ai make a game ect and while Ai is getting pretty good at this its not realistic. You need to know what you want, what to tell it to do ext. Also sometimes you have to tell it how to fix a problem  it won't figure out itself. It is a great tool though and speeds a lot of things up.

Good luck with your MMORPG that is an ambitious project.
